coaching.headline: TwinBlast killed the allied duo fourteen times and took the duo inhibitor; the allied side lost eight structures and took two.

flags.text: Fed TwinBlast like a fucking buffet: Revenant died ten times, eight to TwinBlast, four outside detected fights.
The last allied Fangtooth cost Steel, Scarlett and Yurei, and Greystone took the offlane outer right after.
Yurei: eight deaths on a 4.6 norm and the game's lowest gold, 10168 against Aurora's 12328.
Wraith was the damn bright spot: 15 kills, two deaths, 49121 hero damage, the most in the game.

focus.title: Starve TwinBlast, take Fangtooth at full strength
focus.action: When TwinBlast is unseen, Revenant and Steel concede duo-lane ground until Yurei or Wraith arrives, and the team starts Fangtooth only with all five allies alive.

19.3.call: Won 4-1 just after the duo inner tower and inhibitor fell, with Wraith killing TwinBlast and Dekker, yet no structure or major objective followed before the next fight. With TwinBlast dead, push the duo lane.

24.7.call: Lost 1-3 on the allied offlane as the enemy duo outer fell: Greystone killed Scarlett, Dekker killed Wraith, and Greystone took the offlane inner next. When Greystone sieges a lane, defend as five.

28.1.call: Lost 1-3 at 4v5 after Yurei died on mid outside any fight; Dekker killed Wraith and Greystone killed Scarlett on the enemy offlane, then the allied offlane inhibitor and Core fell. A body down this late, defend the base.

0fe1b802-81f8-4410-b411-4078ca24afa1: Cleared five wards, the game's most, and dealt 477 hero damage per minute against a 274 norm. Before each Fangtooth, sweep the pit the same way.
Two deaths at the Fangtooth pit and one on mid outside any detected fight right before the last 4v5. Enter objective pits only beside Wraith or Scarlett.
Genesis Core went to the enemy with no ally dead. When Genesis Core is up, call all five to the Genesis Core before farming a camp.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c: Brought the damage: 926 hero damage per minute on a 562 norm, first blood on Greystone and a duo-lane kill on TwinBlast. Repeat that rotation while both offlane towers stand.
Greystone took all three offlane structures, scored two of three deaths here and finished 14502 gold to 12524. After the offlane outer falls, call a teammate before the inner.
6b5b62b0-3277-4f79-b99e-32c69ee0ca27: Gold fell 10717 to TwinBlast's 17208 despite 6.1 CS per minute against a 5.1 norm. When TwinBlast has kill pressure, farm under the duo tower until Wraith rotates.
A rotation kill on Aurora on mid answered the jungler's death there, and the allied Fangtooth followed. When an ally falls on mid, rotate in the same way.
b2a3e95e-7fee-40ea-a646-19274373d54b: Six of TwinBlast's seven deaths, and five rotation kills before the enemy mid outer fell, three on TwinBlast. Keep hunting the duo lane whenever TwinBlast scores there.
Both deaths came to Dekker on the offlane after the mid outer fell. When Dekker is unseen on the offlane, let Scarlett engage first.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Mitigated 43666 damage, the game's most, but all six deaths went to TwinBlast, two before minute ten. When TwinBlast is unseen, stay beside Revenant, not ahead.
Three wards on a 6.2 norm while Dekker placed 16; Sanctification raises the ward cap to three. Before Fangtooth or Mini Prime, fill the cap around that pit.
Died on mid in the enemy half outside any detected fight, and the next fight, at Fangtooth, began 4v5. Before an allied objective, hold the allied side of the river.

matchup: Aurora was the jungle opponent and scored one of the eight Yurei deaths; The Fey, Dekker and TwinBlast scored two each.
Aurora's E roots inside a Ring of Frost, and the R slows, then stuns.
build: Manta Scythe, Nightfall and Malady replace the whole winning core of Solaris, Mindrazor and Infernum.
Nightfall heals abilities for 6% of hero damage and grants a shield on takedown.
Malady's Demise adds damage on hitting a hero below 40% health; takedowns reset the cooldown.
eternal: Weald fires true-damage missiles after damaging a hero below 30% health.
Lotus leans ahead in the Yurei jungle field; Weald ranks third of four Eternals with enough games.
Forage with Taproot has too few games to rank; Dryad's Boon with Wind-Rider is the best Weald pair.
augment: Soul Weaver gives Soul Storm 20% damage reduction, plus 5% per hero hit, and a 10% lower cooldown.
Ephemeral Surge leans ahead in the Yurei jungle field; Soul Weaver ranks last of three.
crest: Eviscerator's active grants attack speed, 8% omnivamp and empowered basic attacks for 6s.
Eviscerator has too few Yurei jungle games to lead; Ortus leans ahead of Witchstalker.
Eviscerator evolves from Sharpshooter Crest, Ortus from Assassin Crest.
improvement: Ephemeral Surge over Soul Weaver is the field-backed swap: mana and movement speed from destroying Torn Spirits, giving up the damage reduction.
Lotus over Weald is the field-backed Eternal test, giving up the low-health true-damage missiles.

matchup: Greystone was the lane opponent: first blood went to Scarlett, but Greystone finished 14502 gold to 12524.
Greystone's R enters Stasis and restores health scaled by missing health; Greystone healed 22868, the game's most.
build: Tainted Blade cuts target healing 45% for 3s on physical damage, a direct answer to Greystone's healing.
None of the 50.2% winning core, Alternator, Earthshaker and The Perforator, made the build.
eternal: Marrow heals a share of hero damage, more at low health; The Maw adds true damage below 40% health.
Knell is clearly the field's best Scarlett offlane Eternal; Marrow ranks second.
Leech with Jealousy is the best Marrow pair; Blood Bank with The Maw ranks fourth of five.
augment: Volcaic Slam leaves an eruption after Empowered Cindara that damages and slows by 40%.
Volcaic Slam leans ahead in the Scarlett offlane field. Sound keep.
crest: Judgement's Thunder Cleaver active deals area damage and heals on hero hit.
Gravitum leans ahead of Iceskorn Talons; Judgement, the most played, ranks fifth among crests with enough games.
Gravitum and Judgement both evolve from Champion Crest.
improvement: Knell over Marrow is the field-backed Eternal test: armor shred on hits, giving up Marrow's missing-health healing.
Gravitum over Judgement trades the healing cleave for a projectile grounding the first hero hit for 2s.

matchup: Duo was Revenant and Steel against TwinBlast and Dekker; TwinBlast scored eight of ten Revenant deaths.
Before minute ten the allied duo died seven times to the enemy duo's one.
TwinBlast's passive makes the next basic attack fire three times after each ability cast.
build: Terminus and Vanquisher are two of the 60.7% winning core; Tainted Rounds took the Imperator slot.
Tainted Rounds cuts healing 45% for 3s on basic-attack hits, useful against Greystone and Aurora.
Vanquisher executes a hero taken below 5% health.
eternal: Demiurge raises item stats and item-effect damage by 10%.
Lotus is clearly the field's best Revenant carry Eternal; Demiurge ranks third behind Xyris.
Tri-Core with Memory Leak has too few games to rank; Tri-Core with Bloatware is Demiurge's best pair.
augment: Hellfire Blast adds 7% fourth-shot damage and ignores 30% bonus physical armor.
Hellfire Blast is the most played Revenant carry augment but ranks last; Quickdraw leans ahead.
crest: Pacifier's Adrenalize is an active dash empowering the next physical hit, recastable after a kill.
Liberator is clearly the field's best Revenant carry crest; Pacifier, the most played, ranks second.
Liberator and Pacifier both evolve from Sharpshooter Crest.
improvement: Liberator over Pacifier is the field-backed crest swap: a cleanse and shield in a ten-death game, giving up the dash.
Quickdraw over Hellfire Blast buys faster reloads, giving up the fourth-shot armor ignore.

matchup: The Fey was the mid opponent: six Wraith kills on The Fey, and The Fey never killed Wraith.
Dekker scored both Wraith deaths, each on the offlane.
Dekker's RMB bomb stuns in a small area, longer with distance traveled.
build: Tainted Trident cuts healing 45% for 3s on physical damage; Greystone healed 22868 and Aurora 21186.
The Perforator ignores 30% of physical armor.
The listed core of Soulbinder, Noxia and Wraith Leggings wins only 45.4%, so no core swap is proven.
eternal: Lotus leans ahead in the Wraith midlane field; Weald ranks sixth of seven Eternals with enough games.
Forage with Wind-Rider is the field's best Weald pair on Wraith midlane, so the minors stay.
augment: Sniper's Bounty adds gold on Knock, Knock! killing blows, 40 for heroes.
Sniper's Bounty is clearly the field's best Wraith midlane augment. Sound keep.
crest: Ortus's Limit Breaker grants movement speed and physical power for 7s, with permanent power from takedowns.
Witchstalker and Liberator lead a toss-up in the Wraith midlane field; Ortus ranks fourth among crests with enough games.
improvement: Testing Lotus in place of Weald follows the field lean and trades away the low-health true-damage missiles.
Witchstalker over Ortus adds a cleanse and a max-health empowered hit, giving up the movement and power burst.

matchup: Duo was Steel and Revenant against Dekker and TwinBlast; TwinBlast scored all six Steel deaths.
Dekker's E fence stops enemy heroes passing through, and the RMB bomb stuns.
Dekker placed 16 wards to three from the allied support.
build: Xenia and Dynamo are two of the 54.8% winning core; Frostguard replaced Gaia Greaves.
Frostguard cuts an attacker's attack speed when hit by basic attacks, a fit against TwinBlast.
eternal: Krix adds max health; Regenerative Tissue regenerates health after 8s without hero damage.
Knell, Pilow and Idrisil lead a toss-up for Steel support; Krix, the most played, ranks fourth.
Regenerative Tissue with Cannibalism is the best Krix pair, so the minors stay.
augment: Heavy Metal adds magical damage to Heavy Punches and Shield Bash from 10% of total armors.
Heavy Metal leads a toss-up with Colossal Crash in the Steel support field. Sound keep.
crest: Sanctification's Safeguard shields nearby heroes and adds 50% tenacity while the shield holds.
Leafsong is clearly the field's best Steel support crest; Sanctification, the most played, ranks second.
Leafsong and Sanctification both evolve from Warden Crest.
improvement: Leafsong over Sanctification is the field-backed crest swap: ally speed and slow immunity, giving up the shield and tenacity.
No item change is proven; Gaia Greaves, the third winning-core item, also carries physical armor.

synergy: Little hard CC on our side — we can't force a pick. Play for poke/objectives and punish their cooldowns, don't flip coin-toss 5v5s.
We have sustain (Steel) — favor the longer fight where our heals out-grind them.
Our damage is 4/5 physical — predictable; the enemy itemizes one armor item against most of it. A magical pick would split their defenses.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.

ourKits.combo: Anima Burst / Whispering Echoes apply Soul Rip → Severance resets on Soul-Ripped targets → Soulstorm pulls them in
ourKits.winCondition: chain Severance resets to stick to a target and burst in melee
ourKits.passive: casting grants ranged empowered basics + attack speed
ourKits.playWith: follow-up CC to hold the target she dashes onto
ourKits.playAgainst: her chain needs Soul Rip resets — peel/disengage breaks it; punish when Severance is on cooldown

ourKits.combo: Scar mark → Obliterate homing missiles → Reckoning 1v1 realm ult
ourKits.winCondition: Reckoning a target into the Nether Realm and crit them down 1v1
ourKits.playWith: a team to clean up if his 1v1 stalls
ourKits.playAgainst: the ult is a 1v1 — peel the realmed ally can't help, so don't be caught alone; he's crit-reliant early-weak

ourKits.combo: Peekaboo! mark+slow → Knock, Knock! sniper → Back It Up! displacement ult
ourKits.winCondition: land long-range snipes on marked targets and reset on takedowns
ourKits.playWith: engage that holds a target in his sniper line
ourKits.playAgainst: close the gap — he's weak point-blank; dodge the skillshot snipe

ourKits.combo: Bull Rush knockback → Force Shield wall → Shield Slam knockup+stun ult, Shield Bash %hp
ourKits.winCondition: peel the carry with walls/knockups or engage with Shield Slam
ourKits.playWith: a carry he can wall for and peel
ourKits.playAgainst: his Force Shield blocks projectiles — reposition around it; bait Shield Slam

enemyKits.combo: Vortex Grenade → Vaporize pierce → Rocket Dash reposition → Ventilate ult
enemyKits.winCondition: reposition with Rocket Dash and unload Ventilate from safety
enemyKits.passive: abilities grant AS + a triple-shot next basic
enemyKits.playWith: a frontline to create his free-fire window
enemyKits.playAgainst: he's mobile but squishy — CC through the dash, then burst

enemyKits.combo: Stasis Bomb stun → Photon Disruptor slow → Containment Fence wall → Ion Strike slow ult
enemyKits.winCondition: lock a target with stun + fence and let the team collapse
enemyKits.passive: Rocket Boots mobility, refreshed by abilities
enemyKits.playWith: burst that converts her stun/fence into a kill
enemyKits.playAgainst: dodge Stasis Bomb; the fence zones — flank around it

enemyKits.combo: Assault The Gates leap → Make Way armor shred → Sacred Oath empowered basic → Stone Forged Soul stasis ult
enemyKits.winCondition: front-line aggressively and reset the fight with the stasis heal
enemyKits.playWith: a team that fights while he soaks and stasis-resets
enemyKits.playAgainst: don't waste burst into his stasis — wait it out; anti-heal cuts the ult heal

enemyKits.combo: Boreal Sweep slow → Hoarfrost root → Glacial Charge engage → Cryoseism stun ult
enemyKits.winCondition: chain frost CC (slow→root→stun) to lock the fight down
enemyKits.playWith: burst that converts her long CC chain into kills
enemyKits.playAgainst: she's a CC battery — cleanse/QSS the Cryoseism stun; spread to avoid the chain

enemyKits.combo: Bramble Patch slow → Harvest Nettles stacks → Untamed Growth DoT → Fly Trap pull ult
enemyKits.winCondition: Fly Trap a clumped team and detonate AoE on the pull
enemyKits.passive: takedowns spawn growths + grant move speed
enemyKits.playWith: engage that clumps for her Fly Trap
enemyKits.playAgainst: spread out vs the pull; she's squishy — dive her
